To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
industry leading auditors are more likely to disclose internal control weaknesses prior to the SOX-mandate, while auditors with longer client tenure are less likely to disclose such weaknesses.

industry leading auditors are more likely to disclose internal control deficiencies prior to SOX mandated audits and that longer client-audtor tenure is associated with less disclosure of internal control deficiencies prior SOX mandated audits.

companies audited by industry-leading auditors are more likely to disclose internal control deficiencies (i.e. weaknesses in internal control) and that companies with greater auditor-client tenure are less likely to disclose such internal control weaknesses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
whether the external auditor influences ICD disclosure prior SOX-mandate.
how external auditor characteristics influenced the likelihood of ICA disclosures prior to SOX mandated audits, holding constant whether the company had a control weakness.
the influence of external auditors on the reporting of ICDs prior the SOX mandated audit of internal controls.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
auditors' influence on internal control reporting prior to SOX is mixed.

the findings are consistent with external auditors being more likely to report internal control deficiencies prior to the 2004 audit if they are the industry leading auditor or if they have a long tenure with the client.

external auditors are more likely to disclose control weaknesses when the client is a new client, when the client-auditor relationship is shorter, and when the external auditor is a leading industry auditor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
external auditors influence ICD disclosure, even in a pre-SOX environment.
the external auditor's role in the evaluation of internal control and the disclosure of internal control deficiencies prior to SOX was not as extensive as it is currently.
the audit industry is a highly regulated profession and the external auditors' behavior may be influenced by the regulators.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the external auditor's characteristics influence the likelihood of disclosure prior to SOX.
the external auditor's role is more than just an independent check on the accuracy of a firm's financial statements.
auditors have a role in influencing internal control reporting prior to SOX.
